result.title: Evaluating Cross-Signal Coherence in Mammography Vision-Language Models
result.summary: As vision-language models (VLMs) move toward interpreting medical images directly, their outputs increasingly include not just a label but a stated confidence and a written justification. Yet the field still predominantly evaluates VLMs using just accuracy. We evaluate the coherence between answer, confidence, and explanation across four VLMs on breast density and BI-RADS categorization, using two mammography datasets. We perform controlled perturbations of the question, multiple choice option orders, and the images and assess changes in the three outputs. Our results suggest confidence does not decrease even as the mammography image is changed. Shuffling the options also changes most VLMs' answers. Notably, there are cases where a model's own stated reasoning contradicts its final answer, a distinction accuracy alone cannot capture but one that governs whether an AI-generated answer can be trusted.

AI.brief_summary: 在乳腺密度与 BI-RADS 任务上评估四种 VLM 的答案、置信度与文字解释之间的一致性，通过改动问题、选项顺序和图像等受控扰动观察三者如何变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 该诊断直接考察「解释与最终答案相互矛盾」以及图像改变后置信度不下降等现象，与 LVR 关注的推理轨迹是否真正使用视觉证据、如何评价忠实性与证据敏感性相关，可供核查其扰动设计能否区分证据使用与捷径。
